newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Industry Min. to promote share issues.
newsitem.headline: Russian Industry Min. to promote share issues.

text.p: Russia's Industry Ministry is working on a plan with the Federal Commission for the Securities Market to help companies issue shares, a senior ministry official said on Friday.

"We are concluding an agreement with the commission on developing an infrastructure to assist enterprises in industrial centres," Sergei Mikhailov, who heads the ministry's department on investment and restructuring, told a news conference.

The measures would help enterprises prepare to issue shares on the stock market, he said. Mikhailov added it was part of the ministry's overall programme to provide financial support for struggling enterprises.

The ministry also has concluded general cooperation agreements with Russia's Bank Menatep and Uneximbank to attract more financial credits and investment funds for industrial companies, Mikhailov said. The agreements aimed partly to solve the problem of enterprise debt, he said.
Similar agreements are ready to be signed with 13 other major banks and the ministry is negotiating agreements with 12 other major institutions, he said.
He estimated investment in industry this year would be 140 trillion roubles, most of which would come from the enterprises themselves. Foreign investment would probably be around $5 million, he said.
Mikhailov condemned moves in the State Duma to restrict foreign investment. "There is no money in the federal budget, and for that reason we have to find money in the private sector," he said.
